Subject: Hosted API SLOs - ask re: p50/p95 measurement window and carveouts

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the routing and fallback options. Before we move forward we need a clear statement of the Hosted API latency commitments for the US region. Specifically:

- Can you confirm p50 and p95 targets you commit to for the Hosted product? We need them per-route where applicable (short prompts vs long-context generation).
- We are concerned about the measurement window for p95. Our production traffic has frequent short spikes during end-of-day processing and we need to understand whether those transient spikes will trigger an SLO breach.
- Would Redwood consider a temporary amendment to the measurement window (shorter sliding window / transient carveouts) for the first 90 days post-cutover? This is a key ask to get procurement approval.

I've attached our internal latency samples and Q1 report for your reference (hosted_latency_report_q1.pdf). Procurement will want an addendum to the MSA if there are any non-standard SLOs.

Key business ask: if Redwood can offer a 90-day transitional rule for p95 measurement (or an explicit carveout for burst traffic tied to request size/batched jobs), Procurement can move to an accelerated term and increase committed spend.

Appreciate a concrete proposal we can share internally.

Thanks,

Hi Rita — appreciate the context and the report. Quick summary of what we can offer and a small transitional policy we think is fair: 

1) Baseline Hosted API commitments (US region):
   - p50 (short prompts, <= 256 tokens): 30ms
   - p50 (longer contexts, > 256 tokens): 75ms
   - p95 (short prompts): 220ms
   - p95 (longer contexts): 500ms
   These are for standard single-request routing (no synchronous long-batch jobs).

2) Measurement windows & transitional carveout:
   - Standard measurement: rolling 24-hour aggregation with p50/p95 computed on per-request latencies (we measure at the Redwood ingress per token/response).
   - Transitional 90-day rule (trial period): allow a 10-minute sliding-window carveout for p95 calculations for traffic spikes that meet the burst criteria (>=5x baseline QPS sustained for >2 minutes) OR for requests > 2k tokens (server-side batched processing).
   - After 90 days we revert to the standard 24-hour measurement; we will provide daily dashboards and an automated alert feed to Aperture's SRE during the trial.

3) Remediation and fallbacks:
   - We will enable automatic fallback to a lower-latency model variant for routes that show sustained p95 violations, with a configurable routing policy.
   - For contractual purposes we can add a mutually-agreed addendum specifying the trial rule and the metrics that qualify for the carveout.

I have attached a proposed SLO addendum for legal (proposed-slo-addendum.docx) and the Q1 latency report back for our analysis. If that looks reasonable, we can route the addendum to legal and send a DocuSign link.

Proposed next step: if Procurement agrees, Redwood can accept a 90-day transitional carveout tied to the criteria above in exchange for a 12-month committed spend at the tier we discussed.

Best,

Subject: Fwd: Hosted API SLOs - Aperture Health - recommended stance

Team — forwarding Aperture's ask and my reply. High level notes for product/pricing/legal: 

- Aperture wants a contractual 90-day transitional rule limiting p95 exposure during cutover; they explicitly tie accelerated procurement to that concession.
- My proposal above defines a 10-minute sliding-window carveout for the p95 that only triggers under well-defined burst criteria (>=5x baseline QPS for >2m) OR for very large requests (>2k tokens). This keeps our long-tail risk bounded.

Questions/concerns:
- Product: Is the 10-minute carveout per-route or cluster-wide? Practicality: we can implement tagging per-route and compute qualifiers per logical route — that's slightly more compute but feasible. Karthik, do you foresee any telemetry or billing issues?
- Cost: Allowing a carveout could increase initial load and spikes; we should size expected delta. Ben — can you run a quick cost delta for 3 months at projected Aperture growth (they had sample data attached)?
- Legal/Pricing: Marissa, if we accept, legal will want very explicit language limiting the carveout to the criteria and automatic reversion after 90 days. Also need to be explicit about what constitutes a "breach" during the trial.

Recommendation: Accept the 90-day rule with strict, measurable qualifiers, require Aperture to sign an addendum committing to the 12-month spend and to provide a named SRE contact for alerting.

Thanks — Mina

Hi Rita — thanks for the quick turnaround. Aperture's asked-for concessions are acceptable on our end under the terms described below.

Confirmed items for the addendum: 
- Baseline commitments (US hosted): p50 short 30ms / p95 short 220ms; p50 long 75ms / p95 long 500ms.
- Transitional rule: 90-day period starting on the go-live date. During that period, Redwood will exclude from p95 calculations requests that match BOTH of the following qualifiers:
    a) traffic spike qualifier: >=5x Aperture's baseline QPS for the route sustained for >2 minutes (per-route evaluation); OR
    b) request size qualifier: single-request response >2000 tokens (server-side batched/long jobs).
- Carveout mechanics: the carveout is applied per logical route (per-route evaluation) and computed on a 10-minute sliding window for the purposes of p95 calculation only. All incidents will be visible in the shared SLO dashboard; Redwood will publish a daily digest for Aperture SREs for the trial period.
- Reversion: automatic reversion to standard rolling 24-hour measurement after 90 days.
- Commercial consideration: Aperture agrees to a 12-month committed spend level (as discussed) in exchange for the transitional rule; the addendum references the committed spend tier and termination conditions.

Next step: I'll route the proposed addendum to your procurement/legal team via DocuSign. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/xyz/abcdef (placeholder). Please provide a named legal contact so we can speed execution.
